item.title: The Trinary Dream Endures
item.description:
📝 ) Tri­nary didn’t make any headway in the 20th century; binary’s direct map­ping to the “on”/”off” states of elec­tric cur­rent was just too effective, or seductive; but remember that elec­tric cur­rent isn’t actually “on” or “off”. Tri­nary is philo­soph­i­cally appealing because its ground-floor vocab­u­lary isn’t “yes” and “no”, but rather: “yes”, “no”, and “maybe”. Tri­nary might still have its day.
🔗 Read more: https://www.robinsloan.com/lab/trinary-dream/

item.title: When Pollution Spikes in Southeast Asia, Rainfall Shifts from Land to Sea
item.description:
📝 When Pollution Spikes in Southeast Asia, Rainfall Shifts from Land to Sea Haze over Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Sergei Gussev New research finds that heavy pollution in Southeast Asia is suppressing rainfall over land while intensifying it over the ocean. They found that when pollution spikes, rainfall grows up to 50 percent more intense over the ocean.
🔗 Read more: https://e360.yale.edu/digest/southeast-asia-aerosols-rainfall?asds
